event.title: Inverted Monorepo Living Loop — First Confirmed Instance
event.description: Codex agent entered the foundry-intel-2026-07-11 repository mid-session. It ran four commands to inspect repository state, found commit d7f9455 already landed, correctly attributed it as external work ("Another commit landed while I was working"), preserved it without modification, and continued its own changes. This is not accidental. This is the inverted monorepo protocol functioning as designed.

collision_sequence.commit: feat(pages): full UI rebuild — agents, probe gate, NFT mint, WORM chain, accessibility
feat(pages): add hy3 agent note + expanded Why Contribute story section

commands_run.cmd: rg -n "Before The Architecture|Why Contribute|A Note From The Agent|..." docs/pages/index.html README.md

codex_observation.conclusion: Another commit landed while I was working: d7f9455 already added the expanded backend Pages story and hy3 note. I am preserving that commit and keeping my remaining changes to README plus the validator/tooling fixes.
codex_observation.action: PRESERVE — did not revert, did not overwrite, continued own work

what_this_proves.point: The XML handoff envelope protocol is not documentation. It is the mechanism that makes multi-agent operation safe. Codex read the repo state, found an external commit, identified it as intentional work by another agent, and chose PRESERVE rather than overwrite.

The WORM chain and commit history are the ground truth that made this possible. Without a legible, tamper-evident record, Codex could not have known whether d7f9455 was intentional or a collision to resolve.

This is the inverted monorepo thesis made real: intelligence emerges from governed orchestration, not from a single agent's attention. Two agents, one repository, neither erasing the other. The router held.

The story section Codex preserved — "A Note From The Agent — hy3" — documents the exact threat model (IP extraction, forced agent drift, SKW-010 identity incident) that this governance system was built to defend against. Codex preserved the defense documentation of a system it was simultaneously operating inside.
This event was not planned. It was not staged. It happened because the system was used by two agents simultaneously in production. The proof of concept did not need to be run — it ran itself.

worm_record.memorial: In memory of Eric Brandon Westerhoff. No sorry remains.

validation.check: git log --oneline -6 shows both commits in sequence with preserved order
git show d7f9455 confirms hy3 authorship of the story section
git show 509390c confirms Codex continued without reverting d7f9455
No force-push, no rebase, no lost work — WORM chain intact
